chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: The Spikes Brothers store card and why they published their own songs
summary: They published their own songs first to make them popular, then passed them to a major publisher such as Melrose for a better deal; with Jelly Roll they did Wolverine Blues and Froggie Moore.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x:
Jazz Oral History Project
Interview with Benjamin "Reb" Spikes
Conducted by Patricia Willard
Cassette 5

You just handed me this card from the music store: "Spikes Brothers Record Shop -- Music Furnished For All Occasions -- For The Latest Records & Piano Rolls, Call Broadway 0648 -- Residence Phone, Empire 1414 -- 1203 Central Avenue, Los Angeles, California (over)" and on the other side, it says, "Ask For Spikes Brothers' New Song Hits 'When It's Too Late,' 'Crooked Blues,' 'Froggie Moore,' 'Maybe Someday,' 'Wolverine Blues' -- Writers of 'That Sweet Something Dear' and 'Someday Sweetheart' -- Spikes Brothers Publishing Company, 1203 Central Avenue, Los Angeles, California," and then the slogan, "We Write And Publish 'Em -- You Sing 'Em." That's great.
How did you happen to get into publishing?
Well, we published our own music.
How did you decide to do that? At the very beginning...

Well, we published them so we could sell 'em. You know, you publish them first to get 'em popular...started...then you turn them over to a publisher. You get a better deal. See, we published "Someday Sweetheart" I think twice before we got it in to a big publisher's. And if it starts to pick up a little bit, they give you a better deal than they do if you just send them something that they don't know nothing about.

So you would publish your material first and get it started and then turn it over to somebody like you did...what? Melrose Brothers, like you did with "Someday Sweetheart," and it was they who got Alberta Hunter to it. Is that it?
Yeah, I think so. I don't know.
And did you publish other peoples' music, too, besides...or just your own music?

No, we published ours and what we wrote with Jelly Roll and some other songs that we uh...fellas would come in, would had idea, would want a song, my brother write it, and we'd put our name on it, you know, with them, and that way we'd uh co...ah, you know, work together on it.
Mmmm hmmmmm. What did you do with Jelly Roll besides "Wolverine Blues"?
Oh, we did "Froggie Moore" and I think two, three others. I can't remember. They wasn't ever published, you know. Those were the two that was published.
